question: which river runs through the city of Marlbridge

passages.title: Marlbridge
passages.text: Marlbridge is a market town of about forty thousand people. The river Vell runs through the centre of the town and is crossed by three bridges, the oldest of which gives the town its name.

passages.title: Vell (river)
passages.text: The Vell rises in the Carrow hills and flows east for ninety kilometres before joining the estuary at Portsend. Marlbridge is the largest settlement on its course.

passages.title: Carrow hills
passages.text: The Carrow hills are a low range of sandstone uplands. Several small rivers rise on their eastern flank, including the Vell and the shorter Ashe.

question: what year was the Portsend lighthouse first lit

passages.title: Portsend lighthouse
passages.text: The lighthouse at Portsend was first lit in 1834 and automated in 1971. It stands at the northern end of the harbour wall.

passages.title: Portsend
passages.text: Portsend is a port at the mouth of the Vell estuary. Its harbour wall was completed in 1829, five years before the lighthouse was lit.

passages.title: Harbour walls of the eastern coast
passages.text: Several harbour walls on the eastern coast date from the 1820s. Portsend and Ashcombe were both completed in that decade.

question: Which metal did the Ashe valley smelters work with almost exclusively?

passages.title: Ashe valley smelters
passages.text: The smelters of the Ashe valley worked almost exclusively in tin, drawn from the shallow workings on the valley floor. Copper was smelted only briefly and never at scale.

passages.title: Ashe (river)
passages.text: The Ashe is a short river rising in the Carrow hills. Its valley held a cluster of small smelting works from the sixteenth century onward.

passages.title: Tin working
passages.text: Tin was the principal metal of several inland valleys, worked from alluvial deposits before deep mining became practical.

question: What is the name of the oldest bridge in Marlbridge?

passages.title: Bridges of Marlbridge
passages.text: Three bridges cross the Vell at Marlbridge. The oldest is the Marl bridge, a stone arch of the fourteenth century, from which the town takes its name.

passages.title: Marlbridge
passages.text: Marlbridge grew around a crossing of the river Vell. The crossing was rebuilt in stone in the fourteenth century.

passages.title: Stone arch bridges
passages.text: Stone arch bridges of the fourteenth century survive in several market towns, often carrying only foot traffic today.

question: In which hills does the river that runs through Marlbridge rise?

passages.title: Marlbridge

passages.title: Vell (river)
passages.text: The Vell rises in the Carrow hills and flows east to the estuary at Portsend.

passages.title: Ashe (river)
passages.text: The Ashe also rises in the Carrow hills but flows south, joining the Brent below Southwick.

question: What is the occupation of Hensley Ward?

passages.title: Hensley Ward
passages.text: Hensley Ward was a cartographer who surveyed the Vell estuary between 1841 and 1849. Her charts of the Portsend approaches remained in use for sixty years.

passages.title: Survey of the Vell estuary
passages.text: The estuary was surveyed in the 1840s. The resulting charts were engraved in Portsend and sold to coastal traders.

passages.title: Portsend
passages.text: Portsend is a port at the mouth of the Vell estuary, with a lighthouse first lit in 1834.
